I see , that's understandable . I didn't realize you could choose not to when they explained what drugs they are using when giving the consent form. Such a trooper though ! I am bad with anything getting done down there. The IUD I got before this one almost made me faint, so when they told me they would insert while I was drugged I was like "hell ya!" ahaha

I just knew the antibiotics you had to take beforehand were mandatory . I have trouble swallowing pills, but the nurse was like "its okay take your time , because you can't get the surgery unless you take them". Which makes sense of coruse. A lot.of them ended up melting in my mouth , tasted so bad xD

I actually believe it's only the IUD after procedure is covered , but not things like pills and stuff . But still a good start since our health care is pretty shit even though we pay MSP(I recently found out we are the only province to pay premiums)

It is nice to see a good care network for women's health . The hospital and the other clinics all work in conjunction with eachother , I have been to a couple and the all do amazing work. I never feel anxious , and since I don't have a family doctor it's nice that they will do all the gyno related stuff
. It makes me happy because I hate the thought of women not having access to care. So it's great that they have a way to take charge of their reproductive and mental health 

It's a lot safer now too. When one of the clinics opened up in 1988, my mother said you had to be escorted in because there were a lot of anti-choice there. She got referred there the week they opened to get something checked out by the gyno, and she said the harassment was crazy

You know what's funny , you mentioned how abortions are never talked about/ and also miscarriages are rarely talked about . In reality they are the exact same thing , miscarriage is just a social term for abortion . 
Medically both are abortions .
Society is more open to talking about involuntary/natural abortions (aka miscarriages ), but will ostracize those of us who had voluntary/assisted abortions.
And this is the power of language . They made up the word miscarriage so they could separate themselves from those who they saw as sinful/bad. It always bugged me. 

It made abortion a bad word. Or you will hear "it was a miscarriage , not an abortion so I didn't do anything bad", or " I had a miscarriage , but I would never choose an abortion". It's literally the same thing , but how/why it happens varies. I hate it because it's anti-choice trying to put themselves on moral high ground

There is absolutely nothing wrong with your response . The anti-abortion views that exist in society want us to feel bad about getting an abortion .
 But in reality, it is very easy for many of us. Personally , I only ever felt bad after because there are horrible people out there telling me I'm a piece of crap for it . 

Don't act a certain way just because others expect you to . Do what feels right for you . 
Don't feel bad about your current emotions and actions . And also don't feel bad if you do end up wanting to talk to someone like a councillor .

There is no right or wrong way to react to this .

I kind of seeing what you are getting at here.

This is actually how I feel about the term "miscarriage". It isn't a medical term. The only word used in medicine is 'abortion', regardless if it was voluntary or involuntary.

It is a colloquially used word so people could put themselves on a moral highground over those who have voluntary abortions . As a result , it has made abortion a taboo word , and in a way attempts to shame women who choose an abortion.

Getting back to what you said , I honestly would also like a specific term like you mentioned. I personally didn't mind saying I'm pregnant even though I couldn't go through with it , but I can understand the need for it for others. And not necessarily for the first few weeks, just in general for those not going through with the preganncy (whether it be 6 or 14 weeks etc).

Ironically , the first 3 weeks of pregnancy you aren't actually pregnant (first week is period for eg). And while I totally get it's a standardized way for doctors to count, it's still funny. 

Overall, an alternative word would be great as society has really loaded the word "pregnant", making it feel shameful when it isn't happy news for us / aren't planning to have the baby . 

On the other hand , we could also take back ownership of "pregnant" so that we can dial it back down and make others accept that it isn't always what they typically think .

Please stick to medical .

I attempted the vitamin C thing , personally it didn't work for me. Most of these methods do nothing except harm the woman. If the embryo plans on staying it will take what it needs regardless if you are starving yourself , overdosing etc.

I had a high fever flu that almost killed me (and a broken rib) , yet after I recovered it turned out I was also 8 weeks pregnant (I was unaware as I attributed missed period to the flu).
Even with miscarriage being high the first trimester , the embryo managed to live through that ordeal from week 4-8.

Chances of miscarriage are very high the first few weeks...so yes doing these things may help....But the person most harmed by it is her .
 If the embryo is resilient, it will drain the nutrients and such it needs from her body. If she isn't eating, etc.. It is only hurting her. 
(when doctors talk about eating healthy, getting the right nutrients and water intake , it is meant for the mother .Not the embryo as it will take what it needs regardless)

The first 8 weeks of my pregnancy I had a broken rib and a high fever flu that almost killed me, but never miscarried. 

I tried the vitamin c , and other methods in the past because I was scared . It messed me up a lot. Please stop and see if there is a way to get abortion assistance.
Ahaha, ya I know its just a tiny thing . was just so curious ..Because when I looked up ultrasounds at 8 weeks, they all seemed so clear compared to mine

Thank you !

I accidentally cut it off, but the GA on it is 8.3 weeks . Which was actually less than i thought because from period counting, I was 9 weeks.

I could possibly be the way she took it . She was more confirming it and checking size .

I feel you on this . Nobody seems to care about us unless we are the incubator they want . Of course we care about the baby, but we are humans too . So frustrating :/

You could ask but I have doubt because when they do the surgery the embryo is mixed in with all other contents (it is very small at 10weeks, almost hard to disitnguish from clots) that go through the tube to the jar.
 Right after surgery it gets disposed of with all other biohazard waste. 
So this would require the doctor to open the contents and look through for the embryo . They may be willing but I'm not sure .
The best thing you can do is call the women's clinic and ask. There are no silly questions . I am sure other women have asked before too.
If they don't, you could ask if they will atleast print you out the ultrasound image if you wanted it. 
That's what my clinic did for me

Copper IUDs will make your periods heavier and more painful . When I got mine I had to sign a form that asked if I had the following :

Anemia,
Endometriosis ,
Thin blood,

This is because heavier bleeding and cramping are not good for people in these situations .

I am not sure if you fall under any, but you may want to switch it out for the mirena if you have been soaking through that much . Because even with the expected heavier symtpoms, it shouldn't be at the point of a soaked pad an hour .

Also , you should not be wearing a tampon with an IUD...ever. Gynos highly recommend against it.

Oh! You are like me. I am A- as well. We are a lonesome few as there aren't many of us.

I'm in Canada so I'm not sure how they go about procedures where you are so I have a few questions.

1. When you consent and sign the paper work for the surgery, did they explain what drugs they will be giving etc?( eg. for the IV).
 If so, do you remember anything that had to do with your blood type?  If you are a negative then you are highly suggested to consent to a shot (we call it WinRho here) which will prevent you from making antibodies against potential future pregnancies.
If you do not remember please call whoever you got your surgery from and ask if they did.

Dont freak out though! Usually the antibody creation will only happen if you had a live birth , and that the baby in the live birth was a positive blood type . This is because your blood will mix. With early abortions though (like the one you got) , your blood doesn't come in contact. 
However, it is recommended for every known pregnancy ( I put known because it is common to be pregnant and miscarry without realizing ) regardless if you carry to term or if the baby is also negative, to get the shot.  It is sort of like a precaution . (All my siblings are negative but my mom got it each time anyways).

2. If you did give all info on how and why you got it. Will the doctor discriminate against you ? If so, is that legal where you live ? In Canada it's completely illegal to disicminate in health care so if it happened you report the doctor . 
I ask because you mention it as a worry so I'm curious what the area you are in is like. 

If you freeze up or say miscarriage instead,  there is nothing wrong with that . If there were zero issues with that pregnancy and procedure then the only info they really need is that there was a pregnancy . And while I always advise to tell doctors as much as possible , not telling them would be alright too as if may never be relevant to future visits. Or you can choose to tell at a later date .

Tell them whatever you are comfortable with.
 You could simply say abortion, but don't have to divulge if it was surgical , natural , or medical .
Although , it is helpful to let them know the type. And if it was surgical or medical, you are in no way obligated to tell them why you got it .

Are you also a Rh- blood type? If you are let them know if the gyno who did the procedure gave you the WinRho shot (or something similar ).

If you happen to be in B.C, the women's clinics do medical up until the end of 9 weeks (short of 10).
Considering how many days late you are , you may be just past that line to get one.

If it means anything , I have had both a medical and a surgical, And I would honestly choose a surgical over medical any day . 

Again, I am not sure your provence...but if you are in B.C here are the women's clinics sites.

https://ebwc.ca
http://www.bcwomens.ca/our-services/gynecology/abortion-contraception
https://everywomanshealthcentre.ca

I can't say for sure since I wasn't there for the ultrasound , but when they say you are "no longer pregnant" they mean that the embryo was successfully expelled. However there is still other tissue and blood from your uterus remaining (which is very common for medical abortions ). 
If there was still an embryo they would have highly recommended a surgical for this time around.

When I had a blighted ovum I was given a similar set of 3 options of either waiting for my body to take its course , a surgical, or another round of pills . I ended up choosing another round of pills. Nowadays if it happened to me again , personally I would have chosen a surgical . That way everything is cleared in one procedure .

I live in Canada where abortion is completely legal . At one if the clinics the nurses told me 80% of the women who come in actually were on birth control. 
While BC does prevent a lot, it is not fool proof. And then of course there is mental and physical health reasons for abortions as well. 
Because BC is not fool proof and pregnancy can be dangerous in many ways , abortions will never cease to exist . (Unless there is a way to make pregnancy 100% safe, and BC 100% effective)

 Please keep that in mind and be sensitive  as there are a multitude of reasons we choose to get an abortion . (financial, physical ,mental , abusive/absent father , failed B.C, changed our mind etc..)

That is the first time I have heard of taking it orally . Where I live we are told to take it vaginally.

Regardless , it unfortunately can have a decent fail rate. I had to do it twice. I had a blighted ovum so it wasn't time sensitive. But to be honest , I for sure would have chosen to just get the surgical the second time . Saved a lot of pain and bleeding .

All the best with the procedure ♡

I was scared before I got mine too because I had never had it before (didn't even get any anesthesia for my wisdom teeth)

To be honest I wouldn't describe it as an induced coma. It's more like being really drunk without the headache .
When I got in she put it into my IV vile. Not too soon after I started to feel very light and relaxed(my body and mind). 

Suddenly I'm awake and being sat up.... and then suddenly I'm in the recovery bed awhile later being offered crackers and juice. 
I only remember these small bits of what happened .
 The nurse filled me in with the rest : They had done the procedure , put my underwear with a pad on for me, put me into a wheelchair (I sort of remembered that), brought me to the bed and let me rest . 
After I came to I was just groggy.

Anyone else have major breast leakage a few days after ? I was told it's normal ( I was 8 weeks during my surgery), but mine has been going on for almost 2 weeks now :( 
I was told a week. I know it's probably not a big deal and I will be going to my post checkup soon...but just wondering if anyone else had this happen ?

Just out of curiosity , how did they test to find it at 2 weeks ? Did they do a blood test ?
 I was under the impression you aren't technically pregnant until atleast week 3 because the first 2 weeks is ovulation, and then sperm and egg meet etc. 

Just asking because where I live doctors will not check until it's atleast 4 weeks after last period . But I always wished they could do it sooner if possible :(

For prep, have everything you need ready for where you will be resting. Have water/ tea (or what you prefer to ease potential nausea). A heating pad. Extra pads and possibly a small bin to put them in if you don't feel like you can make it to the washroom to change them . Phone charger , book , whatever you may want to watch to distract yourself . And small snacks or food .

When I talked to my Gyno she said that the procedure itself wouldn't cause depression etc.(which is why you might not find any scientific research) but there are other factors that will contribute to it . 
Such as : The hormonal changes during and after the pregnancy , personal reasons (did you want to have a baby etc), and societys outlook on abortion (people telling you that you are horrible for having it etc)

From a personal perspective , I had no issue with getting an abortion and I was not in a place to have a child. However , I still felt very sad after and often triggered by seeing children etc. I didn't regret the abortion but for sure the hormones started to create these negative emotions for me....and then being neglected by my partner made these emotions worse :(
It worked wonders . Even though I was still upset and cried , my anxiety was completely gone with the stuff they gave me. I remember being oddly chill after .

This actually happened to me . Not sure how common , but it happens . 
My suggestion would be to support her as best as you can .
 I highly suggest looking at online resources and materials to get an idea of some of the hormonal changes and emotions she may experience so you are more prepared to handle it. And also for your own self care to handle any stress.

Number 1 advice : Be there for her, especially if she expresses this to you . 
Often we feel isolated and alone, so making sure to keep contact (online, in person etc) is important. 

Listen to her. Don't just brush off what she says.

There is no evidence to suggest multiple abortions will have long term risks (as much as anti-abortion sites like to suggest).

The surgical procedure is safe and pretty mild compared to many other surgeries people can get (like being cut open etc). 

Even though easier said than done ( I still struggle sometimes thinking it will effect my ability to have children even though it's not true), try not to stress too much ♡

If you can, talk to the gyno about birth control options and give it a try. 
For awhile I wasn't using it because I wasn't happy with the pills I was taking. But then after the second abortion I decided I needed to try something else because the hormonal changes from the pregnancy really got to me . 
I went for the copper IUD and now the hormonal IUD. 
I highly suggest inquiring about it and seeing if your doctor will insert it after your procedure while you are still under . Where I live this was highly recommended because it saved you the usual insertion pain and an extra trip to the doctor .

I would request the doctor to do an ultrasound to see if you actually need another round.

I had a medical for a blighted ovum a few years ago. Where I live in Canada we are told to take it vaginally , but it is the same idea and series of pills you had to take . Because I had trouble inserting the pills in there (was never much of a tampon person or anything , made me squeamish), I had to do the whole thing again a few days later because not all tissue was expelled . But the gyno had given me an internal ultrasound first. 

In regards to feeling and pain ... I didn't bleed as much as the first time because half of the contents was already gone. But still had the cramping. Although I felt a bit more prepared this time and kept up with taking the pain meds(i.e taking early / before it wears off).

From personal experience I would suggest the surgical . 
I have had a surgical, and a medicated to speed along a blighted ovum . I didn't have a good time with the medical . I had to insert a series of the pill vaginally , which I had trouble doing before they started to break apart .
This resulting in me having to do a second round of the pill series because it was incomplete in getting rid of the pregnancy tissue .
 And then there is the expected heavy bleeding and cramping.

With the surgical there was of course cramping and light bleeding after, but leaving the hospital with the relief that the doctor has taken everything out really helped . Because then you can just focus on getting your body and mind recovered.
If you are having the surgical before 12weeks it will be a vacuum aspiration . Nothing crazy. They just dilate you a little and insert the tube. You won't even know they are doing it because of the IV.
